outcome: Typed extension-request workflow bound to canonical capability identity
owner_impact: Student and Professor research AI can now submit unsupported requirements under the six owner-approved classes with minimal publication identity. All six classes remain Professor-visible and none is automatically rejected. Semantic approvals bind or create canonical capability identity; multiple requests/papers can converge on one canonical capability without using free-text labels as identity. Professor approval still does not authorize implementation.

next.text: #347 is the known successor. It will refactor authoring-contract capability ownership and diagnostic classification without changing simulator behavior or authoring syntax. #347 has not started in this owner turn.

technical_evidence: MCP request interface is vlab.capability-request/4; MCP interface is 12 and server version is 3.4.0.

Request identity is explicit: canonical_capability_id for known semantic targets, existing_request_id for exact request reconciliation, and a proposed generic target only when no canonical semantic capability exists.
All six request classes are accepted into Professor triage, including implementation/optimization and security-boundary requests; no automatic rejection class exists.
Publication title + persistent identifier are stored separately from request reasoning and attach duplicate-safely to canonical semantic capability provenance after Professor approval.

Semantic developer handoff is anchored to canonical capability identity so one engineering issue may advance multiple approved request rows; owner implementation authorization remains outside the research-AI/browser path.
No simulator/kernel/physics/compiler behavior or Configuration/Initialization/Controller/Metrics syntax was changed.
